import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/nls_raw.csv')

# Select the relevant columns
gender_column = 'Sex of respondent, 1979'
degree_completion_column = 'Highest grade completed, 1979'

# Convert the gender column to a categorical variable
df[gender_column] = df[gender_column].astype('category')

# Create a boxplot to visualize the relationship between gender and degree completion rates
sns.boxplot(x=gender_column, y=degree_completion_column, data=df)
plt.title('Relationship between Gender and Degree Completion Rates')
plt.xlabel('Gender')
plt.ylabel('Degree Completion Rates')
plt.show()

# Perform a t-test to determine if there is a statistically significant difference in degree completion rates between genders
male_degrees = df[df[gender_column] == 1][degree_completion_column]
female_degrees = df[df[gender_column] == 2][degree_completion_column]

t_statistic, p_value = ttest_ind(male_degrees, female_degrees)
t_statistic, p_value

# Check for missing values in the relevant columns
missing_values = df[[gender_column, degree_completion_column]].isnull().sum()
print("Missing values in gender column:", missing_values[gender_column])
print("Missing values in degree completion column:", missing_values[degree_completion_column])

# Drop rows with missing values in the relevant columns
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=[gender_column, degree_completion_column])

# Perform the t-test on the cleaned data
male_degrees_clean = df_clean[df_clean[gender_column] == 1][degree_completion_column]
female_degrees_clean = df_clean[df_clean[gender_column] == 2][degree_completion_column]

t_statistic_clean, p_value_clean = ttest_ind(male_degrees_clean, female_degrees_clean)
t_statistic_clean, p_value_clean
